reviews.review:
Warframe is a fun well balanced awesome game! featuring a great multiplayer system with a superb Co-Op mode to enjoy.
 The game is also really optimised playing well on almost any pc out there and it maintained a great framerate even on my brothers old machine that could only handle games like tf2 on low! this is recommended to everyone that's looking for a Co-Op game for a LAN or game night!

7/10 Great Game!

Recommended for the continuous support, nice developers, and because I know there are a lot of people who enjoy this sort of game.
However, after all these hours, I have to say.. it is not a game for me. It is, primarily, a game about items, numbers and RNG. About mindlessly grinding, getting new stuff and seeing your numbers get higher and bars fuller. If that's what you enjoy- more power to you, this game's definitely great for this sort of gameplay. However..

 It always feels like the cycle of grinding, building loadouts, customizing your character/ship/clan dojo, and grinding some more takes precedence over the gameplay itself. Often, enemies will outright one-shot you if you don't have good enough equipment. However, once you get enough of that equipment (mostly mods, these cards you can collect and upgrade through grinding, which are the main source of your equipment's power), you will often one-shot all the enemies. You either can't do much to succeed, or to have fun. This is especially problematic when you play with groups, as veteran players (not blaming them, they're just playing the game the objectively optimal way) will often effortlessly melt most of the enemies, or rush the objective and complete it before you get the chance to do much.

Any new addition to the game feels restricted by this mentality. The big open-world maps aren't much more than a big pre-made map for you to run the same uninteresting missions on. The people inhabiting their central settlements not much more than sources of (in the case of these open worlds often somewhat pointless) items you have to grind new currency to get. The weekly mission system? More objectives to check off and earn spending money from. Events? Yeah, run the same mission dozens, if not hundreds of times to get the stuff you want. Haven't heard good thing about the recently introduced "lich" enemies in this regard, but I haven't played the game in a while, so no proper opinion here.

The atmopshere of the game suffers as well. Genuinely awesome moments will get ruined because of the game's focus on getting big numbers on your guns and characters. Bosses will be unbeatable, or drop like flies. You'll get hunted by an extra rare, supposedly elite assasin squad for assisting their empire's enemies, and.. you'll accidentaly kill them trying to slow them down within the first few shots of your shotgun.

Once again, Warframe is not a bad game, definitely not. There's a lot of content, a lot to obtain and make you feel powerful. The devs, although sometimes seemingly disconnected from their own game and from what the community wants, have time and time again shown that they care much more than your average AAA game company. If you want a game about getting more and more gear and costumizing your character and ship, Warframe is definitely worth giving a shot. 

Also, don't spend money on plat until you get a 75% (or 50%, if you're really desperate) discount from the daily log-in thing. It might take a while if the game expects you to pay up, though. (on the other hand, if you haven't played in a while and pick up the game again, you'll get one in a few days)

Warframe is like Mass Effect and Deus Ex games except it being multiplayer and focuses less in epic quest lines and more in micromanaging your gear and provides faster action. There are loads of warframes and weapons to choose from and mods to customize them. There is no real end game content in the concept of it being something hard you have to pick up the best players and gear and still have a challenge to get trought it. In the other words this game is just fun to play with friends or with the ingame community and doesn't provide much challenges for more demanding hc players (yet). In a nutshell this game is an endless grind for more gear and mods which are ultimately forgotten in your inventory with no use or sold to make room for new ones. That being said it is weird that there's no ingame wiki for drop locations. I don't have a broblem searching info from the internet but the getting of the info shouldn't be the only challenging thing in a game. 

Eventhough all I said sounds a bit negative the game is actually brilliant and worth of trying. The diversity of stuff you can obtain and use is vast. There is a steady stream of new content updates and devs are really open and close to players with their weekly streams and announcements (props!). Bugs are fixed swiftly and servers are up all the time. In the beginning I would have agreed with Metacritics score (68/100). All in all as the game is at the moment I would give it a score of 85/100 while waiting for end game and more stuff to use my overpowered gear. The game has come a long way and is constantly developing. Even if you have played this earlier and got disappointed I recommend to give it a try again.

Looking for a free-to-play Third Person Shooter/RPG game that is not pay-to-win? Warframe is deffinitely worth a try. Despite being still in beta(therefore with some bugs and flaws here and there) it provides genuine fun and sense of power whether you are stomping hordes of enemies with Rhino or sneaking upon someone and slashing enemies while being invisible with Loki. For a free-to-play game all the essential items are possible to get even without shelling out a single cent, where even most of the cosmetic items/options/alterations are possible to obtain without buying them without real-life money, Warframe deffinitely sports a surprising economy aswell.
